entries.title: Hotel furniture and renovation projects
entries.summary: A hotel brings together different uses. Guestrooms need space for luggage, storage and circulation. Public spaces and dining areas need their own furniture choices. We review these requirements using your plans and room schedules.
sections: Define the scope by space
List room types and identify beds, headboards, desks and storage for each type. Schedule public spaces and restaurant furniture separately so proposals can be compared consistently.
Connect furniture with technical planning
Review dimensions, finishes, power points, lighting and assembly access together. Working drawings and samples should be confirmed before the order is approved.
Plan a phased renovation
Specify which areas are available, storage constraints and handover dates. Production, transport and on-site work are separate stages.

entries.title: Office furniture for your workplace project
entries.summary: Workplace projects begin with people and activities. Workstation counts, meeting spaces, circulation and storage needs provide a framework for selection. Hongye discusses configurations and finishes using your layout.
sections: Start with the layout
Specify team size, work patterns and spaces to furnish. Check access routes, door openings and the space around desks and tables.
Coordinate equipment
Define cable routes, displays, power points and conferencing equipment. Visually similar configurations can meet different technical requirements.
Compare specifications
Review dimensions, supports, finishes, adjustments and maintenance needs line by line. Required documents and tests should be identified for the selected models.

entries.title: Furniture for restaurants and social spaces
entries.summary: A restaurant combines guest comfort, staff movement and everyday use. Review seating capacity, table layouts and seat heights before choosing finishes. Lounges and bars need choices suited to their use.
sections: Plan the dining space
Separate two- and four-person tables, larger groups, bar areas and lounge seating. A zone-based schedule connects quantities to the plan.
Choose finishes for the use
Describe cleaning needs, stain exposure, frequency of use and colour references. Performance claims must be supported by documents for the product concerned.
Consider storage
For multifunctional spaces, specify stacking, movement and storage needs. Check access for replacing or maintaining items.

entries.title: Furniture for your villa project
entries.summary: A residential project benefits from an overall view. Room proportions, access, light and daily habits guide furniture choices. Fenmi Casa discusses selections using your plans, references and material palette.
sections: Build a shared direction
Gather style references and identify priority rooms. A palette of wood, fabrics and surfaces can connect living, dining and bedroom spaces without making every room identical.
Check dimensions
Compare furniture footprints with measured plans and access routes. Doors, stairs and lifts can affect handling and assembly.
Define what is included
Separate freestanding furniture, drawing-based items and accessories. Services, samples and delivery conditions are defined through the project brief.

entries.title: Furniture for apartments and private residences
entries.summary: Apartments require careful coordination between furniture and available space. Fenmi Casa discusses pieces, dimensions and finishes within a defined residential project.
sections: Respect the proportions
Review sofas, tables and beds on the plan. Circulation and openings must remain compatible with daily use.
Connect different spaces
Living and dining areas can share a palette while serving different functions. Tell us about existing finishes when discussing combinations.
Plan access
Provide lift dimensions, floor information and building access. On-site services are confirmed for the destination and agreed scope.

entries.title: A furniture contact for residential designers
entries.summary: Working with an interior designer depends on precise information. References, drawings, dimensions and samples provide the basis for coordination. Fenmi Casa helps organise furniture choices and the technical points to confirm.
sections: Structure the selection
Prepare a room-by-room list with references, desired sizes and inspiration images. Separate existing models from items needing further review.
Approve the finishes
Connect each finish with a reference and sample where needed. Decisions and document versions should remain traceable.
Review interfaces
Identify furniture adjoining walls, floors or equipment. Joinery work and local installation depend on the agreed scope, rather than a general promise.

entries.title: Hotel guestroom furniture set
entries.summary: Coordinate beds, headboards, desks and storage with the room type.

entries.title: Buffet and storage furniture
entries.summary: A storage selection for dining and service areas.

entries.title: Restaurant and dining table
entries.summary: Select table formats in relation to capacity and circulation.

entries.title: Bar and high seating
entries.summary: Review seat height against the actual counter and intended use.

entries.title: Workstation and modular layout
entries.summary: Review workstations against your workplace layout.

entries.title: Meeting-room table
entries.summary: Configure the table for room capacity, access and equipment.

entries.title: Reception desk
entries.summary: Review reception furniture around staff tasks and visitor movement.

entries.title: Residential living-room furniture
entries.summary: Coordinate seating and tables around your living-room plan.

entries.title: Bedroom and private-space furniture
entries.summary: Organise selections by room, dimensions and material palette.

entries.title: Furniture selection for private interiors
entries.summary: Coordinate residential furniture using a room-by-room brief.

entries.title: Furniture dimensions and customisation
entries.summary: Customisation connects your expectations with the constraints of the product. Plans, measurements, references and quantities help review options for your project.
sections: Review dimensions
Provide desired sizes, site measurements and wall or equipment interfaces. Feasibility is confirmed for the chosen model.
Record the decisions
Link every change to an item reference and document version. Changes after approval may affect production conditions.
Confirm the scope
Supply, additional studies and on-site work are defined in the proposal.

entries.title: Materials and finishes for your project
entries.summary: Materials are selected for appearance, use and maintenance. We review your references and the documentation needed for the products selected.
sections: Connect appearance with use
Describe frequency of use, cleaning needs and indoor or outdoor conditions. A visual finish alone does not demonstrate performance.
Compare references
Associate material names, colours, surfaces and sample references with the same item. Technical documents are reviewed for the relevant models.
Confirm with a sample
On-screen colour varies with lighting and displays. An approved sample provides a clearer reference for the order.

entries.title: Samples and project approval
entries.summary: Approval can concern a material, finish, drawing or model. Sample requirements are agreed according to the project and chosen products.
sections: Choose review points
Identify what needs review: appearance, dimensions, assembly, equipment or documents. Record the scope in the brief.
Record decisions
Use item references and version numbers for each decision. Avoid contradictory approvals between drawings, messages and samples.
Prepare the next stage
Quantities, finishes and schedule should be confirmed before ordering. Sample conditions and costs are discussed for your request.

entries.title: Preparing packing and delivery
entries.summary: Delivery planning starts with quantities, destination and site access. Transport, receiving and assembly conditions are confirmed within the agreed scope.
sections: Organise the batches
A room-, zone- or phase-based schedule can help identify packages. Specify storage needs and site readiness.
Clarify responsibilities
Transport, customs, taxes, unloading and assembly need separate discussion. A general price or delivery period cannot replace a destination-specific proposal.
Prepare receiving
Identify the receiving location, access and responsible people. Assembly documents and reporting conditions are defined for the order.

entries.title: Preparing a hotel furniture schedule
entries.summary: A useful schedule links each item to a space, quantity and reference. It helps teams review the scope and compare proposals.
sections: Start with the spaces
List room types, then reception, dining, meetings and other included areas. Keep typical-room quantities separate from total quantities.
Describe each item
Include function, desired dimensions, material, finish and quantity. Attach a plan or reference when an item depends on a layout.
Separate the services
Samples, transport, receiving and installation should be identified with their responsibilities. Furniture quotations can cover different scopes.

entries.title: Preparing your residential furniture brief
entries.summary: An initial brief does not need to be complete. It should explain the rooms, preferences and decisions already made.
sections: Describe the rooms
List rooms to furnish and furniture to retain. Measured plans and access dimensions help frame the selection.
Share references
A few style images and a material palette are more useful than many unexplained pictures. Say what you like about each reference.
Identify priorities
Destination, target date and room priorities help discuss the schedule. Delivery and services are defined for your brief.

entries.title: Organising sample approval
entries.summary: Clear approval connects a decision with an item, version and responsible person. This reduces uncertainty across documents.
sections: Identify the reference
Describe the item, material and finish. Record the date and reference of the reviewed sample.
Describe the decision
State whether the sample is approved, requires changes or needs another review. Record specific reservations in the brief.
Keep versions consistent
After a change, verify that drawings and furniture schedules use the same version. Photographs do not replace every physical check.

entries.title: Comparing furniture quotations on a common basis
entries.summary: Quotations are comparable only when their scopes are comparable. A lower total may reflect different materials, quantities or services.
sections: Compare the items
Check dimensions, finishes, quantities and composition. A product name alone does not establish equivalence.
Identify services
Samples, packing, transport, importation and assembly may be included, excluded or priced separately. Check each proposal.
Document open questions
Review substitutions, documents, stage-by-stage timing, payment terms and responsibilities before approval. Estimates must remain distinct from contractual conditions.

entries.title: Information for an office furniture project
entries.summary: The brief should explain who uses the spaces, what equipment is needed and how furniture fits the plan.
sections: Describe activities
Specify headcount, fixed or shared desks, meeting capacity and reception needs.
Define interfaces
Identify cable routes, screens and equipment. Check access and storage.
Prepare specifications
Define desired dimensions, finishes and documentation. Performance is confirmed for selected models.

entries.title: A guestroom composition reference
entries.summary: This image from the group library supports a project discussion. It is not a claim of a completed project in France or Morocco.
sections: Read the composition
Identify sleeping, storage and desk areas. The actual plan and room category determine the selection.
Turn the image into a brief
List items, dimensions and desired finishes. Final materials and composition are confirmed through the brief.

entries.title: A workplace layout reference
entries.summary: This reference from the group library illustrates a workplace setting. It is not presented as a locally delivered project.
sections: Review the functions
Separate workstations, discussion areas and storage. Adapt the layout to your team size.
Define the configuration
Connect each item to plans, dimensions and cable-management needs. Images do not replace specifications.

entries.title: A residential interior mood reference
entries.summary: This image is a visual reference from the group library for discussing your project. It is not a local delivery testimonial.
sections: Identify combinations
Review proportions, colours and relationships between surfaces. Select the elements relevant to your project.
Adapt to your residence
Plans and access routes guide dimensions. Items and finishes must be confirmed separately from the image.

entries.title: Your furniture project in France
entries.summary: HY Mobilier is a French-language contact point for Hongye, a manufacturer in China. Projects in France are discussed using plans, quantities and document requirements. This site does not claim a local factory, store or installation team in France.
sections: A brief for discussion
Designers, owners and purchasing teams can share a space-by-space schedule and required documentation. Conditions are confirmed for each selection.
Specify the destination
Importation, taxes, receiving and assembly need discussion with the project parties. Documents depend on products and supply-chain responsibilities.

entries.title: Furniture for projects in Morocco
entries.summary: A project in Morocco can involve several spaces and stakeholders. Share the furniture schedule, plans and priorities to discuss a coordinated selection.
sections: Separate the spaces
Hotels, restaurants, offices and private residences have different requirements. A zone-based schedule clarifies the scope.
Plan receiving
City, address, access and site readiness help discuss transport and receiving. Local assembly must be defined within the agreed scope.
